request.prompt:
You are clustering code review findings from the same PR. For each PAIR below, decide whether the two findings describe the SAME underlying issue — same root cause in the same code location. Different wording is fine. A finding about a DIFFERENT defect in the same file or function is NOT the same issue. Severity or aspect differences of the same root cause ARE the same issue.


For THIS scoring pass, duplicate equivalence is stricter than sharing a root cause.
You must compare the COMPLETE MATERIAL CLAIMS, including mechanism, triggering
conditions, execution path, and consequence. The same line or broad concern does
not establish equivalence. A report of wrong-category selection, a case/rename
mismatch, a crash, and a silent fallback are different claims even at one lookup.
An inactive/unbound API concern and an alleged active user-facing failure differ.
A compound report with an additional material claim does NOT equal its subset.
Differences only in wording, severity, or hedging do not create separate claims.
If the claimed mechanisms, triggers or consequences conflict, or one report adds
an unsupported/different material factual claim, return same=false. You are NOT
verifying which claim is true; do not repair or reinterpret either report to make
them match. If unsure whether their full claims are equivalent, return false.

For every numbered pair, extract what A and B actually CLAIM into mechanism,
trigger and consequence. Then list material_differences and give your equivalence
verdict, confidence and reason. same=true requires no material differences.
Return ONLY this JSON object, with EVERY pair index exactly once:
{"pairs":[{"pair":1,"a":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"b":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"material_differences":[],"same":true,"confidence":0.9,"reason":"..."}]}

PAIR 15:
A: add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false forces a full posts-table rewrite under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on every PostgreSQL version current at this time (the metadata-only ADD COLUMN default optimization only arrived in PG 11). Operators of large forums — Discourse's target market — hit a hard site-wide outage while db:migrate runs: every request touching posts blocks for the whole rewrite, which takes minutes on multi-million-row posts tables; adding the column nullable and backfilling/defaulting in a follow-up step would keep the table readable and writable during the deploy.
B: add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false forces a full rewrite of the posts table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on the PostgreSQL versions this app runs (constant-default ADD COLUMN only became catalog-only in PG 11). On any forum with a large posts table, rake db:migrate during deploy blocks all reads and writes on posts for the full table-rewrite duration — a sitewide outage window proportional to posts size; adding the column nullable, backfilling in batches, and only then constraining bounds the lock to short scans instead of a whole-table rewrite.

A: Both external fetches (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` here and `open(url).read` in TopicEmbed.import_remote) use open-uri with no open/read timeout. A stalled or slow-loris feed/article server hangs the sidekiq thread indefinitely (open-uri has no default open timeout); with retry: false the hourly poll slot is consumed by the hung thread and repeated hangs exhaust the sidekiq worker pool, stalling unrelated background jobs on the instance.
B: import_remote — the open(url) fetch plus ruby-readability extraction with the tags/attributes whitelist that serves on-demand embedding, TopicRetriever's fetch_http fallback, and the disqus importer — is exercised by no test in the diff. A regression in the readability integration (whitelist option handling, title/content extraction, encoding failures) breaks the primary content-import path only at runtime inside background jobs, invisible to CI and to operators until embeds silently stay stuck on the loading page.
